title: Universal quantification
description: The universal quantification ∀ x1,…,xn · P is true if P is satisfied for all possible values of x1…,xn. A usual pattern for quantification is ∀ x1…,xn · P1 ⇒ P2 where P1 is used to specify the types of the identifiers. — The existential quantification ∃ x1…,xn · P is true if a value of x1…,xn exists such that P is satisfied. — The types of all identifiers x1…,xn must be inferable by P. They can be referenced in P.
types: The quantifiers and the P are predicates.
